blocks.text: The expression translated “the Jews” in John 7 should not automatically be read as a single hostile ethnic group. Its referent can vary with context, including Jewish people generally, Judeans, festival crowds, or particular authorities. Reading every occurrence as the same group can distort the Gospel’s conflicts and intensify antisemitic harm.

John 7:53 has a notable textual history. It is absent from the earliest major Greek witnesses and appears in different places in later manuscripts. It is therefore widely judged not to have belonged to the earliest recoverable form of John, though it has long been received as Scripture.

The crowd’s appeal to David’s descendants and Bethlehem in verse 42 belongs to a Davidic-expectation context in which John reuses or echoes Micah. Matthew and Luke also reuse or echo Micah in related Bethlehem, shepherd, household-conflict, and Davidic-expectation settings.
